verses.text: Now the Philistines had taken God’s ark, and they brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
The Philistines took God’s ark, and brought it into the house of Dagon, and set it by Dagon.
When the people of Ashdod arose early on the next day, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before Yahweh’s ark. They took Dagon, and set him in his place again.

When they arose early on the following morning, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before Yahweh’s ark; and the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands were cut off on the threshold. Only Dagon’s torso was intact.
Therefore neither the priests of Dagon, nor any who come into Dagon’s house, step on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod, to this day.
But Yahweh’s hand was heavy on the people of Ashdod, and he destroyed them, and struck them with tumors, even Ashdod and its borders.
When the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, “The ark of the God of Israel shall not stay with us; for his hand is severe on us, and on Dagon our god.”

They sent therefore and gathered together all the lords of the Philistines, and said, “What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?” They answered, “Let the ark of the God of Israel be carried over to Gath.” They carried the ark of the God of Israel there.

It was so, that after they had carried it there, Yahweh’s hand was against the city with a very great confusion; and he struck the men of the city, both small and great so that tumors broke out on them.
So they sent God’s ark to Ekron. As God’s ark came to Ekron, the Ekronites cried out, saying, “They have brought about the ark of the God of Israel to us, to kill us and our people.”

They sent therefore and gathered together all the lords of the Philistines, and they said, “Send the ark of the God of Israel away, and let it go again to its own place, that it not kill us and our people.” For there was a deadly confusion throughout all the city. The hand of God was very heavy there.
The men who didn’t die were struck with the tumors; and the cry of the city went up to heaven.

footnotes.content: The Philistines hold God's ark as spoil, but they don't yet understand what they've taken. How often we think we've captured blessing when really blessing captures us—we just haven't felt it yet.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They place the ark beside Dagon, as if Yahweh and Dagon were peers worthy of equal standing. Pride always assumes the false gods can share the room with the true God. They never do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dagon falls on his face before the ark—a wordless confession. The idol cannot stay upright in the presence of the living God's throne. Even the gods of stone and wood bow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When they lift Dagon up again, God dismantles him completely—head and hands severed on the threshold. Mercy would have been to let them learn from one fall; instead, God answers their refusal with unbending clarity. His patience is real, but so is His sovereignty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A custom born from shock: they won't cross the threshold where Dagon fell apart. Fear of the threshold becomes their worship. Sometimes we mark the place where we glimpsed the Lord's power, as a way of remembering who He is.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh's hand grows heavy—not like a punishment from outside, but like a truth they cannot bear. Tumors spread among them. The Lord lets their own ground speak the language they need to hear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The people of Ashdod finally see what is so. Their admission—"His hand is severe on us, and on Dagon our god"—carries both panic and a dawning recognition. Even false gods feel the weight when the true God is present.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The lords gather to solve a problem they cannot name. They pass the ark to Gath as if moving it will move the judgment. We do the same—shift the trouble, change the location—but God's hand follows where our hearts haven't truly turned.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: At Gath, confusion descends again—tumors on great and small alike. The Lord treats every city the same way because He sees every life as mattering, and He will not be treated as a trophy to parade.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now Ekron: the Ekronites cry out in terror that the ark has come to kill them. They read the pattern and understand it at once. Sometimes it takes a few cities learning the same lesson before the whole land knows the God of Israel is not capturable.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The lords finally speak what they should have known from the start: "Send it away, that it not kill us." Readers today hear an echo in how long we cling to what we've seized, until clinging costs everything. The Lord's gentler word comes first; judgment comes when we refuse to listen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The cry of the city rises to heaven—a prayer of desperation, but finally a reaching upward. When all else fails and the people cry out, God hears. That cry is the beginning of wisdom, and the threshold of mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
